title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page opens Section XI, 'Récapitulation sur les groupes M_{ρ,σ}', with preliminaries that put the data defining these group schemes into a normal form.

Data. Work over a base scheme S. Let G be a form of GL(2) (for instance the units of an Azumaya algebra M of rank 4, the form of M_2(O_S) attached to G). This gives forms SG of SL(2) and PG of PGL(2). Choose:
- two sections ρ̃ and σ̃ of PG;
- an additive one-parameter subgroup ξ̃_0 : G_a ↪ PG. This is equivalent to a regular unipotent section, or a regular nilpotent section N_0 of M.

The data must satisfy two conditions:
- (1) σ̃ρ̃ = ξ̃_0(1), and ξ̃_0 and ξ̃_1 := ρ(ξ̃_0) = σ(ξ̃_0) are independent on every fibre;
- (2) Tr σ = 0 for any local lift σ of σ̃, so σ̃ is an involution in PG.

This is a scheme-theoretic, parametrised version of the modular group PSL_2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3. There σ = S has order 2, ρ has order 3, and their product is the unipotent T.

Canonical lifts. Lifts ρ, σ to G are fixed by two conditions:
- ε_0 = -σ^{-1}ρ, equivalently ε_1 = -ρσ^{-1};
- Tr(ρ+σ) = 1, equivalently Tr ρ = 1.

Trivialisation. One then builds an isomorphism GL(2) ≅ G, defined by requiring ε_1 = [[1,0],[1,1]]. This forces
- ρ = [[0,1],[v,1]] and σ = [[0,-1],[-v,0]], with v ∈ Γ(G_m);
- det ρ = det σ = -v;
- ε_0 = [[1,1/v],[0,1]].

Consequences, confirmed on the next page:
- ρ² - ρ - v = 0 and σ² = v.
- The commutative algebras A_ρ = O_S[X]/(X² - X - v) and A_σ = O_S[Y]/(Y² - v) give tori T_ρ and T_σ.
- These tori, together with the Borel-type subgroup B'_0 = T_0·L_0, are the building blocks of the groups G_{ρ,σ} and M_{ρ,σ}.

So the moduli of such data is G_m, with coordinate v. The modular case is v = -1, where ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]] has order 6 in GL2 (order 3 in PGL2) and σ = [[0,-1],[1,0]] has σ² = -1. For general v, ρ̃ is a 'generic' elliptic or hyperbolic element; it is not of order 3.

Purpose. This normal form serves the 'équation des lacets' programme. There Grothendieck studies algebraic group-scheme models (the M_{ρ,σ}, with centres computed on the previous page) of the modular group and its relation σρ = unipotent.
errors: Minor inconsistency in normalisation. (1) says σ̃ρ̃ = ξ̃_0(1), while (3) uses -σ^{-1}ρ. These agree in PG because σ̃ is an involution, but in G they differ by the scalar σ² = v. Also ε_0(1) = [[1,1/v],[0,1]], so the parametrisation of L_0 by λ is rescaled by 1/v; the next page indeed writes λ/u. The letter v here becomes u on the next page.

ideas.what: Normal form for a pair (ρ, σ) in a form of GL2 over a base S, with σ an involution in PGL2 and σρ regular unipotent. It is rigidified to explicit matrices depending on one unit v, giving a moduli space G_m with the modular group at v = -1.
ideas.modern_name: Normalisation of SL2/GL2 representations of Z/2 * Z with unipotent product (a parabolic character-variety slice); scheme-theoretic forms of GL2 via Azumaya algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Fricke–Klein trace coordinates; Hecke groups); Azumaya/forms of GL2 standard (Grothendieck, Brauer groups; SGA3)
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts as such. Related themes (modular group, M_{1,1}, Teichmüller tower) appear in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche.

ideas.what: Tori T_ρ and T_σ as unit groups of the quadratic algebras O_S[ρ] and O_S[σ], plus a Borel-type B'_0, used as building blocks for algebraic group models M_{ρ,σ} of the modular group.
ideas.modern_name: Rank-one tori from quadratic algebras; amalgam-type algebraic models / completions of SL2(Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Group schemes of units of quadratic algebras are standard. Algebraic completions of SL2(Z) are associated with Hain (relative completion, 1990s).

missed.claim: The one-parameter family over G_m (coordinate v) of normalised pairs (ρ, σ) contains all Hecke triangle groups. ρ̃ has order n in PGL2 exactly when 1/(-v) = tr²/det = 4cos²(π/n), i.e. v = -1/(4cos²(π/n)): n = 3 gives v = -1 (modular), n = 4 gives v = -1/2, n = 6 gives v = -1/3. So Grothendieck's M_{ρ,σ} construction, done over a general base with general v, implicitly gives an integral-scheme framework interpolating Hecke groups and modular group schemes. The page does not say this, and no such scheme-theoretic treatment is known to me.
missed.quote: ρ = (0 1 / v 1), σ = (0 -1 / -v 0) (v ∈ Γ G_m), det ρ = det σ = -v
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a mild observation. It could frame the M_{ρ,σ} groups as a family of algebraic models over G_m (or over Z[v, 1/v]) specialising to the modular group, which is relevant to relative completions and to arithmetic of Hecke groups. Whether Grothendieck exploited it would require reading further pages.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a recapitulation and set-up page doing explicit, correct linear-algebra normalisation. The broader programme (algebraic group-scheme models M_{ρ,σ} of the modular group over a general base) is unpublished and of some interest, but this page itself contains only routine computations.
transcription_corrections: 'On construit un épi-gl.gr. [?] GL(2) ↠ G' is more plausibly 'On construit un isomorphisme GL(2) ⥲ G'. The arrow carries a tilde (an isomorphism, i.e. a trivialisation), not an epimorphism.
'(v ∈ Γ(G_m) [?])' reads '(v ∈ Γ G_m)', i.e. v a unit on S.
'une section unipotente régulière de ε_0 de ϖ [?]' probably reads 'une section unipotente régulière ε_0 de G'. The inserted '{+ξ_a+}' appears to be ε_0 or ξ_0 written above.
'une section [?] de la forme M de M_2(O_S)' likely reads 'une section nilpotente régulière N_0 de la forme M de M_2(O_S) associée à G'. N_0 lives in M rather than in G.
'additif bordé [?]' is uncertain. It possibly reads 'additif donné' or 'additif borné'; the word before 'additif' (unipotent) is struck out.
Marginal 'Préliminaires' is written diagonally next to 1°; the margin at bottom left is the archive page number 412.
